extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents/applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners (and practitioners) on applying statutory bars and obviousness rejections under 35 U.S.C. §§102 and 103, including provisional rejections, disqualification under §103(c), common-ownership rules, and required contents of Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(e) — Patent to another with earlier filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention was described in a patent granted on an application for patent by another filed in the United States before the invention thereof by the applicant for patent, or on an international application by another who has fulfilled the requirements of section 371(c) before the invention by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded by paragraph 7.07 and may be preceded by one or more of paragraphs 7.08–7.11. See MPEP for use of specific form paragraphs (e.g., 7.15.02, 7.15.03) depending on common assignee/inventor status. If applied, explain whether the reference is being treated as 'anticipated' or 'clearly anticipated' and insert the prior art relied upon; explain basis for earlier effective U.S. filing date of the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(f) — Applicant not the inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection where the applicant did not himself invent the subject matter sought to be patented (i.e., invention was derived from another).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded by paragraph 7.07 and may be preceded by appropriate preceding paragraphs. Insert a full explanation of the supporting evidence establishing that applicant was not the inventor. See MPEP § 2137 for evidentiary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(g) — Priority of invention (interference/earlier domestic invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: (g)(1) during an interference another inventor establishes that before such person's invention the invention was made by such other inventor and not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed; or (g)(2) before such person's invention the invention was made in this country by another inventor who had not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed it. In determining priority consider dates of conception, reduction to practice, and reasonable diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider conception and reduction to practice and diligence of the party first to conceive and last to reduce to practice. This paragraph must be preceded by paragraph 7.07; see MPEP for interference and priority procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(b) — Public use or on sale bar
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) based upon a public use or sale of the invention prior to the critical date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded by paragraphs 7.07 and 7.09 (or 7.103). A full explanation of the evidence establishing a public use or sale must be provided in the Office action (insert in bracket). See Pfaff v. Wells and related MPEP guidance on 'ready for patenting' and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(c) — Abandonment of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) because the invention has been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by appropriate paragraphs (7.07 and 7.10 or 7.103). Insert a full explanation of the evidence establishing abandonment of the invention. See MPEP § 2134 for guidance on abandonment evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(d) — Foreign patenting by applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(d) as being barred by applicant's foreign patenting (or earlier foreign filing) that makes the subject matter available under 102(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded by paragraphs 7.07 and 7.11 (or 7.103). Include appropriate dates and explain how they make the foreign patent available as prior art under 102(d). See MPEP § 2135.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a 35 U.S.C. 103 (obviousness) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection, the examiner should set forth: (A) the relevant teachings of the prior art relied upon (with specific citations where appropriate); (B) the differences between the claim and the applied reference(s); (C) the proposed modification(s) of the applied reference(s) necessary to arrive at the claimed subject matter; and (D) an explanation why one of ordinary skill in the art at the time would have been motivated to make the proposed modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To establish a prima facie case of obviousness, the examiner must show (1) some suggestion or motivation to modify or combine references (in the references or in common knowledge), (2) a reasonable expectation of success, and (3) that the references (alone or combined) teach or suggest all claim limitations. The teaching/suggestion and reasonable expectation must be found in the prior art and not based on applicant's disclosure. Cite In re Vaeck and see MPEP §§2141–2144.09 for examples and decision law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's obligation to present motivation/line of reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial burden is on the examiner to provide some suggestion or motivation for combining references and to present a convincing line of reasoning why the artisan would have found the claimed invention obvious in light of the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References relied upon, even if in a minor capacity, should be positively included in the statement of the rejection (see In re Hoch). Provide reasoning examples per MPEP §2144–§2144.09 and Ex parte Clapp. Avoid relying on applicant's disclosure to supply missing motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of written record and explanation of rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must properly communicate the basis for a rejection so issues are identified early and the applicant can fairly reply; written rationale is important for later interpretation since patents are presumed valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because examiners cannot normally be compelled to testify about mental processes, the written record must clearly explain the rationale for decisions during prosecution. Include sufficient explanation so that the scope and basis of any rejection are clear (see MPEP discussion on presumption of validity under 35 U.S.C. 282).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 (copending applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional rejection of obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 is appropriate where copending applications have different effective filing dates and a common assignee or a common inventor, because the earlier filed copending application, if patented, would constitute prior art under 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional rejection alerts applicant that an actual rejection may follow if one application issues and gives applicant opportunity to respond. It may be overcome by: (A) arguing patentability; (B) combining subject matter into a single application claiming 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit and abandoning copending apps (subject to 112/120 support requirements); (C) filing a 37 CFR 1.132 showing derivation; (D) filing a 37 CFR 1.131 showing earlier invention date; or (E) filing a continuation after Nov. 29, 1999 that shows common ownership per amended 103(c). A terminal disclaimer cannot overcome certain provisional situations (see In re Bartfeld). Confidentiality under 35 U.S.C. 122 must otherwise be maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional double patenting and conflict between copending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claims of the copending application conflict with claims of the instant application, a provisional double patenting rejection should also be made (use paragraphs 8.30 and 8.32).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the MPEP illustrate when provisional double patenting rejections and provisional 102(e)/103 rejections apply. If inventions are commonly owned and requirements are met, some rejections may be overcome (e.g., terminal disclaimers), subject to statutory/precedential limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of continuing application claiming 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: An application claiming the benefit of a prior-filed copending national or international application under 35 U.S.C. 120 must name as an inventor at least one inventor named in the prior-filed application, and the prior filed application must disclose the named inventor's invention claimed in at least one claim of the later-filed application in the manner required by 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: So long as at least one inventor is in common and other requirements are met, the Office will permit a claim for 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit without additional submissions. The examiner must examine the earlier-filed application to determine common inventorship and 120 requirements when necessary (e.g., when intervening references appear).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 103(c) — Disqualification of prior art for common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter developed by another which qualifies as prior art only under one or more of subsections (e), (f), and (g) of section 102 shall not preclude patentability under 103 where the subject matter and the claimed invention were, at the time the invention was made, owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective Nov. 29, 1999 the amendment expanded disqualification to include prior art under 102(e) for applications filed on or after that date. 103(c) applies only to obviousness determinations under 103 and does not affect anticipatory prior art under 102. The burden to establish disqualification (i.e., common ownership) is on the applicant (or patentee) once the examiner establishes a prima facie case of obviousness. See MPEP §706.02(l) for procedural details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of 103(c) — what is not disqualified
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter that qualifies as anticipatory prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102 (including 102(e) used as anticipatory) is not disqualified by 103(c). If subject matter qualifies as prior art under other subsections (e.g., 102(a), 102(b), or 102(e) as anticipatory), it will not be disqualified under 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 103(c) affects only prior art insofar as it is used in an obviousness (103) rejection. Do not apply 103(c) to prevent rejections under 102; be careful to determine the statutory basis of the prior art being relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'common ownership' for 103(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Commonly owned' means wholly or entirely owned (100%) by the same person, persons, or organization at the time the claimed invention was made; less than 100% ownership of subject matter or the claimed invention means common ownership does not exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common ownership requires actual ownership or a legal obligation to assign both the subject matter and the claimed invention at the time the claimed invention was made. A license where basic ownership rights are retained does not defeat common ownership. Moral or unenforceable obligations do not evidence common ownership. Determination is fact-specific; see examples in MPEP (parent/subsidiary scenarios, joint ventures, government inventor rights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden and nature of evidence to establish common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden of establishing that subject matter is disqualified as prior art under 103(c) rests on the person urging disqualification (e.g., applicant or patentee). The showing must establish that common ownership existed at the time the later invention was made; a statement of present common ownership is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable showings per 37 CFR 1.104(a)(5) include: (i) application files referring to assignments recorded in the PTO conveying entire rights to same person; (ii) copies of unrecorded assignments conveying entire rights filed in each application; (iii) an affidavit/declaration by the common owner stating common ownership and facts explaining the basis, signable by a corporate official; or (iv) other evidence establishing common ownership. See In re Onda and related precedent for evidentiary sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure when common ownership is alleged
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner will consider copending applications to be owned by the same person if the necessary showing under 37 CFR 1.104(a)(5) is present; otherwise earlier inventions are not disqualified as potential prior art under 102(e)/(f)/(g) as they apply through 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application file(s) establish common ownership at the time the later invention was made, the examiner need not examine grounds based solely on 102(e)/(f)/(g) as they apply through 103; otherwise, make appropriate 102(f)/102(g) or 103 rejections. See MPEP §706.02(l)(2) and §706.02(l)(3) for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants' duty of disclosure when inventorship/common ownership differs
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors of subject matter not commonly owned at the time of invention but currently commonly owned may file as joint inventors; applicants have an obligation under 37 CFR 1.56 to point out inventor and invention dates and the lack of common ownership at the time the later invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent evidence to the contrary, the examiner will assume applicants comply with their duty of disclosure. Foreign applicants combining subject matter from related applications with different inventors into a single U.S. application should provide information on invention dates and common ownership to enable correct application of 103(c) and 102(f)/(g)/103 rejections. See MPEP guidance on 119 benefit and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of references relied upon in rejection statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reference is relied on to support a rejection, whether or not in a minor capacity, that reference should be positively included in the statement of the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the reference with appropriate column/page/line references where relevant (see In re Hoch). Properly include all relied-upon references to allow applicant to respond and to preserve record for later proceedings.
